A.explanation: This is the contact force at Y, found from moments about X, not the larger force required at X closer to the $700\text{ N}$ man.

B.explanation: This is half of the total $900\text{ N}$ downward weight and ignores that the $700\text{ N}$ man is much closer to X than to Y.

C.explanation: Taking moments about Y gives $R_X \times 20.0 = 700 \times 14.0 + 200 \times 10.0$, so $R_X = 590\text{ N}$ upward.

D.explanation: This is the sum $700\text{ N} + 200\text{ N}$ and ignores that the load is shared between supports X and Y.

hints: Notice the distances from support X: the $700\text{ N}$ man is at $6.0\text{ m}$ and the uniform $200\text{ N}$ beam acts at its centre at $10.0\text{ m}$.
To find the force at X, take moments about Y so the unknown force at Y has zero moment and is eliminated.
The clockwise moment about Y from X must balance the anticlockwise moments of the $700\text{ N}$ weight at $14.0\text{ m}$ from Y and the $200\text{ N}$ weight at $10.0\text{ m}$ from Y.
walkthrough: Identify the forces and positions: support X at $0$, man $700\text{ N}$ at $6.0\text{ m}$ from X, beam weight $200\text{ N}$ at the midpoint $10.0\text{ m}$ from X, support Y at $20.0\text{ m}$ from X.
For equilibrium the resultant moment about any point is zero. Choose Y as pivot so only $R_X$ and the two weights contribute.
Distances from Y are $20.0 - 6.0 = 14.0\text{ m}$ for the man and $20.0 - 10.0 = 10.0\text{ m}$ for the beam weight.
Set sum of moments about Y to zero: $R_X \times 20.0 - 700 \times 14.0 - 200 \times 10.0 = 0$.
Calculate the load moments: $700 \times 14.0 = 9800\text{ N m}$ and $200 \times 10.0 = 2000\text{ N m}$, total $11800\text{ N m}$.
Solve for $R_X$: $R_X = 11800 / 20.0 = 590\text{ N}$ upward with correct unit $\text{N}$. This is option C.
